findings: Nine frames arrive; eight have a sole-indirect topology receipt. Frame 6 is the first complete desktop. No received frame shows Run; Run appears only on the restored ordinary display. Notepad input is never sent.

Two failures creating Level Zero command queues return ZE_RESULT_ERROR_UNKNOWN; a later fence synchronization reports ZE_RESULT_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST. There are 440 successful NPU results and exactly matching positive acknowledgements, plus two negative responses. The final device-loss request has no completed response.

The four complete captured draws all pass CPU replay. After NPU recovery they all pass on the physical NPU, with complete output byte-identical to CPU; the first capture differs from the independent mathematical oracle in one component by one byte, on both devices.

The observer stops on a DWM DDI rejection, waits its bounded 450 seconds for the topology helper, and removes both custom drivers. The helper never records a final restoration result. The ordinary desktop is visually verified after device removal.

The NPU worker is terminated by the stream controller but remains retained and output collection blocks. A first NPU replay times out. An exact-instance NPU restart using Windows PnPUtil succeeds and releases the blocked controllers; two replays during recovery fail platform auto-detection before the fourth succeeds. A subsequent fresh four-capture NPU replay passes completely.

The device restart preserves driver 32.0.100.5540 and does not request a system reboot or touch the GPU. This is a runtime/device-state failure, not evidence of a newly unsupported shader. Resource accumulation is a hypothesis requiring controlled tests; no command-queue capacity limit has been established.
Full desktop offload, usable interaction, physical scanout migration and Tahoma improvement remain unverified.
